rationale: The causal control ran (CheckRun 68ee55636577494e915fce091da4d876, exit 0) and settled the one way the regression could still have been wrong. The control is the witness scenario with a single variable removed: the same node, the same instrumented store, the same real depose heartbeat and the same held-open election write, but nothing delivered while the write is held. It reports the gate opened with the term still reading 3 and the persisted term reading 3, and after the release the term and persisted term are 4 with the node leading - a monotone step, no regression. So the held write does not lose the term by itself, and the falls recorded in the two witness runs (13 adopted in memory and in the stable store, then 5 persisted) are attributable to the empty heartbeat written on the fast path from outside the main loop, which is exactly the cause the account names. That closes the causal gap: the two witness runs show the regression is reproducible, and this control shows it is not an artefact of how the harness holds the window open. I record the control observation as its own fact, add the answer to the same investigation with all three receipts joined, and restate the account with the competing explanation excluded rather than merely noted.

knowledge.statement: On one real single-node Raft instance with the same instrumented store used by the term-regression witness, the election's term write was held open with the term and the persisted term both reading 3, and when it was released without any heartbeat being delivered the term and the persisted term became 4 and the node reached Leader state - a monotone step, with no fall below the held term.
knowledge.conditions: Captured snapshot 09193ea9b7ee4df99810e6eee7058028; identical setup to the witness harness (in-memory transport wrapped for the heartbeat fast path, instrumented stable store, single-voter bootstrap, a real empty heartbeat to depose the node) with the only difference that nothing is delivered during the hold.

interpretations.rationale: The control was queued to exclude the only competing explanation I could not remove by reading: that my instrumented store, by holding the write open, loses the term by itself and the heartbeat merely happens to be present in the witness runs. It does not: with everything else identical and nothing delivered during the hold, the term and the persisted term go from the held 3 to 4 and the node leads - monotone, no fall. Compare that with the witness runs, where the same hold is interrupted by one empty heartbeat carrying term 13 that the node adopts in memory and in the stable store, and where the term and persisted term afterwards are 5, below the term already adopted and recorded. With the control in hand the attribution is causal within this scenario rather than merely plausible: the fall requires the off-main-thread write, and the two witness runs show it is reproducible while the control shows it is not an artefact of the instrumentation. That is the strongest form this claim can take without a real multi-node deployment: the elements are a transport whose heartbeat fast path runs appendEntries on the connection goroutine, a node whose election has read its term and not yet stored the next one, and a heartbeat arriving inside that interval - and the ordering is permitted by code that has no guard around the read-modify-write pair, with the durable store recording whichever write lands last. The counterweights stand as previously recorded: the interval is microseconds wide in production and the harness only widened it, the heartbeat comes from the wrapper rather than the network transport, the runs are single-voter so the peer-side consequences remain the conditional account already answered, and the fast path's guard still keeps entries and the commit index out of the empty heartbeat so this is not a route to divergent logs.
counterevidence: The control shares the harness and the instrumentation with the witness runs, so it excludes the instrumentation as the cause of the fall but not every harness-specific factor; what it cannot show is the interleaving under the network transport's own scheduling.
All three executions use one cluster shape and one scenario, so the causal attribution holds within that scenario rather than as a general rate of occurrence.
The witness's higher term was delivered by the wrapper transport, which mirrors the network transport's classification and dispatch instead of exercising its socket path.
The single-voter configuration makes every step after the stale write deterministic, which is why the witness runs agree exactly; with several voters the aftermath could resolve differently.
limitations: Three executions, one scenario: reproducible and now causally controlled, but the probability of the interleaving under real scheduling remains unmeasured.
The control exercised the same instrumentation path that the witness used, so it speaks to the cause of the fall and not to the internals of the store beyond holding the write.
The peer-side consequences of a regressed term remain the conditional account already recorded, since none of the three executions has a real peer at the higher term.
interpretations.joint_history: The three receipts are the same scenario with one variable: identical setup, identical instrumentation, identical depose, identical held-open election write. In the two witness runs an empty heartbeat carrying term 13 is delivered on the fast path while the write is held; in the control nothing is delivered during the hold. They are separate executions of one scenario, so the comparison supports causal attribution within this scenario and does not extend it to other cluster sizes or to the network transport's socket path.
